name: Ala-Bel Pass
near: There are no permanent villages by the pass. Taldy-Bulak is ~18 km as the crow flies (OSM marker, catalog calculation); to the north are the villages of the Suusamyr Valley, to the south through the Chychkan gorge (~30 km) are the Toktogul Reservoir and Toktogul.
elev: 3175 m (Nomad's Land, Trip to Kyrgyzstan, central-asia.live, trvlland). Some guidebooks give 3184 m — not confirmed by the sources found.
short: Ala-Bel (3175 m) is the highest point of the main Bishkek — Osh highway in the Talas Ala-Too: a pass between the Suusamyr Valley and the Chychkan gorge, with alpine meadows in summer and a snowy “white desert” in winter.
desc: Ala-Bel Pass lies in the Talas Ala-Too at an elevation of 3175 m and is considered the highest point of the main Bishkek — Osh road (travel2unlimited; Nomad's Land). It connects the Suusamyr Valley with the valley of the Chychkan River, which flows parallel to the road south toward the Toktogul Reservoir. The ascent and descent are relatively gentle; in summer the slopes are covered with alpine meadows with flowering grasses, and in winter the pass is buried in snow (Trip to Kyrgyzstan). The stretch of highway from km 198 to km 255 (Ala-Bel and the Chychkan gorge) is one of the most avalanche-prone in the country: on 28.01.2026 an avalanche at km 247 blocked traffic in both directions (economist.kg).
guide: Ala-Bel is the main “ceiling” of the north-south road: here you climb above 3100 m without leaving your car. Stop at the top — in summer the meadows are bright with flowers and smell of herbs, and beyond the pass the green Chychkan gorge begins, with a rushing river alongside the road. Even in July it can be cold and windy here, so keep a jacket handy. In winter, don't plan the crossing without checking the Ministry of Emergency Situations (MChS) and Ministry of Transport bulletins — the 198–255 km stretch is regularly closed because of avalanches. If altitude makes you feel unwell, don't linger at the top for long.
see: The 3175 m saddle with views of the snowy peaks of the Talas Ala-Too; alpine meadows in bloom (June — July); the descent into the Chychkan gorge with the river alongside the highway; the Suusamyr Valley on the northern side (Trip to Kyrgyzstan; Nomad's Land).
skip: If you aren't driving the Bishkek — Osh highway, it isn't worth making a trip just for the pass — it is a photo stop. In winter, when there is avalanche danger, it is better to postpone the crossing or fly Bishkek — Osh.
diff: Easy: a stop on a paved highway, no walking section. The 3175 m altitude can cause mild altitude sickness if you stay for long (editorial).
when: June — September: flowering meadows, dry road. The highway is formally open year-round, but from December to March avalanches, black ice and closures are possible (the avalanche of 28.01.2026 at km 247; MChS warning 31.01–02.02.2026 for the 198–255 km stretch — economist.kg).
hours: Open 24 hours, a section of the state highway. Temporary closures during avalanches and snowfalls; restrictions for trucks have been introduced at Ala-Bel (Kaktus). Check the Ministry of Transport and MChS bulletins before a winter trip.
daytime: Morning and the first half of the day — less cloud over the pass and better visibility; in winter, drive only in daylight (editorial).
how: Along the Bishkek — Osh highway: from Bishkek via Kara-Balta, the Too-Ashuu tunnel and the Suusamyr Valley (about 4 h by car, estimate; the pass is at roughly km 200–210 — based on MChS data about the avalanche-prone 198–255 km stretch, to be verified). From Osh/Jalal-Abad — north via Tash-Kumyr, Kara-Kol, Toktogul and the Chychkan gorge. Highway tunnel toll: 50 som for cars with Kyrgyz plates / 200 som for foreign ones (since 01.01.2024), at the Sosnovka and Kara-Kol checkpoints.
needcar: Yes: your own/rental car, a taxi, or a seat in a marshrutka (minibus)/shared taxi along the highway (a stop at the pass is by arrangement with the driver).
self: Yes: a paved highway, no permits. In winter — only with winter tires and when the road is open.
roadtype: Paved mountain highway Bishkek — Osh (EM-02/M41); the ascent and descent are gentle (Nomad's Land), in winter snowdrifts, black ice and avalanches on the 198–255 km stretch (economist.kg, 2026).
traveltime: From Bishkek — about 4 h to the pass (estimate; 5–6 h to the Chychkan gorge per avtoprokat.kg); from the pass to Toktogul — ~1.5 h (estimate).
stay: There is no lodging at the pass. The nearest options: the Chychkan tourist base/hotel (~km 240, $51–58 for a standard room, per 2026 checks of the Chychkan gorge), the Oson motel in the Chychkan gorge, guesthouses and yurt camps in Suusamyr, hotels in Toktogul (via toktogulvisit/CBT Toktogul).
net: Not confirmed for the saddle. In the neighbouring Chychkan gorge there is no signal or it is limited (too.kg). No reports about operators at the pass were found.
entry: Free: a section of the state highway. Only the toll for the tunnels of the Bishkek — Osh highway is paid (50/200 som since 01.01.2024).
transfer: Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Toktogul 400 som, shared taxi 600–800 som, private taxi 3200–5600 som (toktogulvisit); shared taxi Bishkek — Osh ~2500 som/seat (2026).
bring: A warm jacket and hat even in summer (3175 m), sunglasses, water; in winter — chains/winter tires, and a reserve of fuel and food in case the highway is closed.
warn: Avalanche-prone stretch 198–255 km (Ala-Bel and the Chychkan gorge): in winter the highway can be closed (avalanche of 28.01.2026); when driving through, keep a distance of at least 500 m (MChS recommendation, 2026). The 3175 m altitude — altitude sickness is possible. The weather changes quickly, and snow is possible in summer. Stop only at safe pull-offs — there are many trucks on the highway.
food: On the highway in the Suusamyr Valley in summer, kumis and dairy products are sold at yurts (typical for the highway; specific places at the pass are not confirmed). Cafes are in the Chychkan gorge and Toktogul.
reviews: Google Maps: 4.6 from 59 ratings (catalog check, 10.2026). Travelers note the views, meadows and snow; cons — cold, wind, winter closures (travel2unlimited, trvlland).
p.sum: Ala-Bel (3175 m) is a photo stop on the Bishkek — Osh highway, about 4 h drive from Bishkek; you get here by your own/rental car or by marshrutka (minibus)/shared taxi to Toktogul with a stop by arrangement. In summer, overnight in the Chychkan gorge or Toktogul; in winter, check the MChS bulletins before setting out: the 198–255 km stretch is avalanche-prone, and trucks are not let through during blizzards.

p.iti.1.title: A combination
p.iti.1.plan: Bishkek — Ala-Bel — Chychkan gorge — Toktogul Reservoir (overnight) — Naryn canyon — Arslanbob. From here, via Otmok, it is also logical to continue to Talas (Besh-Tash, Manas Ordo).
p.season: June — September: greenery, flowering (June — July), cold and windy even in summer, snow possible. October — November: first snowfalls. December — March: avalanches at 198–255 km, blizzards, restrictions for trucks.
p.budget.economy: Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek — Toktogul 265–400 som; a night in a CBT house in Toktogul ~$13–24.
p.budget.comfort: Car rental $20–100/day + fuel + tunnel toll 50/200 som; a night at Chychkan $51–58.
p.permits: Not needed. Tunnel toll on the Bishkek — Osh highway 50 som (Kyrgyz plates) / 200 som (foreign plates) at the Sosnovka checkpoint.
p.access: From the car — accessible to everyone. At 3175 m: people with heart problems and small children should not linger. With a dog — no problem.
